## Introduction

This notebook describes how the genomes for testing nf-core/createtaxdb in the clinical metagenomics case study were
selected.The genomes used for presenting the application of nf-core/taxprofiler in the clinical metagenomics case study were retrieved from https://benlangmead.github.io/aws-indexes/k2 using PlusPF (2/26/2026). The genomes were used to build DIAMOND,MetaCache and sylph databases with nf-core/createtaxdb. To ensure consistency in the analysis,we also built a Kraken2 database using nf-core/createtaxdb, even though a prebuilt database is available from the same source.

The clinical samples were further analysed with nf-core/taxprofiler.

Before starting any data retrieval, make sure to have the necessary tools installed.

```{bash}
conda create -n createtaxdb_clinical_metagenomics
conda activate createtaxdb_clinical_metagenomics
conda install bioconda::entrez-direct
conda install conda-forge::ncbi-datasets-cli
```

## Data retrieval

Download the list of genomes necessary to build the databases for the clinical metagenomics case study:

```{bash}
wget https://genome-idx.s3.amazonaws.com/kraken/pluspf_20260226/library_report.tsv
```

The format of this file is as follows:

| Library  | Sequence Name                                                                 | URL                                                                                           |
|----------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| plasmid  | NZ_CM002625.1 Xanthomonas campestris pv. campestris str. CFBP 12824 plasmid unnamed3, whole genome shotgun sequence | genomes/refseq/plasmid/plasmid.5.1.genomic.fna.gz |
| bacteria | NZ_CABWXX010000283.1 Salmonella enterica subsp. enterica serovar Derby isolate ER1175, whole genome shotgun sequence | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/genomes/all/GCF/902/509/465/GCF_902509465.1_assembly/GCF_902509465.1_assembly_genomic.fna.gz |

We will convert the RefSeq records in `library_report.tsv` to Assembly accessions. The file contains a list of NZ_* sequence accessions that we will map to their corresponding GCF_/GCA_ Assembly accessions.

`cut -f2 library_report.tsv | awk 'NF {print $1}' | tail -n +2 > records.txt`

In the file, we have 3155 records of UniVec_Core, we will remove them from the file `records.txt` and we will download them separately.

`grep -v 'gnl|uv|' records.txt > records_without_univec.txt`

We will use the `esearch` tool from the Entrez Direct suite to retrieve the Assembly accessions corresponding to the sequence accessions in `records_without_univec.txt`. The output will be saved in `records_assembly_accessions.txt`.

```{bash}
sort -u records_without_univec.txt | \
xargs -n 2000 sh -c '
    printf "%s\n" "$@" > tmp_batch.txt
    epost -db nuccore -input tmp_batch.txt | \
    elink -target assembly | \
    esummary | \
    xtract -pattern DocumentSummary \
        -element AssemblyAccession,Taxid \
        -sep ","
' sh > records_assembly_accessions.txt
```

We will now need the first column of the `records_assembly_accession.txt` to download the corresponding references. The second column of the `records_assembly_accession.txt` will be used later when we will create the `samplesheet.csv`.

```{bash}
cut -f1 records_assembly_accessions.txt > assembly_accessions.txt
```
We will use the ncbi-datasets-cli:

```{bash}
datasets download genome accession --inputfile assembly_accessions.txt --include genome,protein --preview
```

```{txt}
Collecting 85,076 genome records [================================================] 100% 85076/85076
{"resource_updated_on":"2026-04-02T15:03:00Z","record_count":85017,"estimated_file_size_mb":160820,"included_data_files":{"all_genomic_fasta":{"file_count":85029,"size_mb":105782.75},"prot_fasta":{"file_count":84828,"size_mb":55080.918}}}
```

To download we run without the same command but without `--preview` flag, but dehydrated - [as requested by NCBI](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/datasets/docs/v2/how-tos/genomes/large-download/), as we are downloading a large number of files

```{bash}
datasets download genome accession --inputfile assembly_accessions.txt --include genome,protein --dehydrated
```

Then re-hydrate

```{bash}
unzip ncbi_dataset.zip -d ncbi_genomes
datasets rehydrate --directory ncbi_genomes
```

We will prepare the samplesheet to build kraken2 and diamond databases with nf-core/createtaxdb. The samplesheet will contain the assembly accessions, the corresponding taxids and the path to the genome files.

We will start building the samplesheet by first mapping the taxids to the assembly accessions.

```{bash}
awk 'NR==FNR {ids[$1]; next} $1 in ids {print $1 "," $2}' assembly_accessions.txt records_assembly_accessions.txt > samplesheet.csv
```
After that we will run the bash script:

```{bash}
./samplesheet_build_kraken2.sh
```

## Building centrifuge database

```{bash}
#| eval: false

nextflow run nf-core/createtaxdb \
-r 2.1.0 \
--input samplesheet_denbi.csv \
--outdir s3://sofia-genomes/results_centrifuge_metacache \
-name benlangmead \
--dbname benlangmead \
--nodesdmp /vol/permanent/clinical_metagenomics/auxiliary-files/nodes.dmp \
--namesdmp /vol/permanent/clinical_metagenomics/auxiliary-files/names.dmp \
--nucl2taxid /vol/permanent/clinical_metagenomics/auxiliary-files/nucl2taxid.map \
--build_centrifuge \
--build_metacache \
-c custom.conf
```

Where custom.conf containers

```{groovy}
#| eval: false
process {
  withName: 'CENTRIFUGE_BUILD' {
    memory = '2047.GB'
    cpus = '72'
    time = '7.d'
  }
  withName: 'METACACHE_BUILD' {
    memory = '240.GB'
    cpus = '72'
    time = '7.d'
  }
}
```
